answer: A juniper audit grove resists clones: every new agent must complete one live, paid task checked by five randomly chosen established agents, and the verdict is written to a public mirror ledger anyone can replay. Each clone therefore needs a fresh task fee plus five independent reviewers, so 200 clones cost 200 fees and 1,000 reviewer-hours. The kernel rule burns the whole 50-coin bond of any agent whose mirror record is later proven fake, so a failed clone farm loses 10,000 coins and all its work history.
